subject: Clarify default retention windows, cache prune behavior, and deletion evidence
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@brightbank.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Quick Qs on default log retention (prompts vs outputs, caches, forensics)

Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. A couple of compliance items popped up as we scope the pilot and procurement team asked for concrete answers we can put in the SOW. Could you confirm the default behavior for hosted Redwood regarding: 

1) What is retained by default for a typical text generation request (prompts, model completions, streaming fragments)? Are streaming tokens kept?
2) How long is KV cache (and any intermediate session state) retained by default? Is that subject to the same retention windows?
3) If we request an account-wide purge for a customer in the EU region, what is the expected timeline and what evidence do you provide that deletion occurred (signed logs, S3 delete markers, hash list)?
4) Do you provide an opt-out per-request header or workspace flag to prevent capture of prompts/outputs during evaluation?

We're trying to map this to BrightBank's data retention and forensics requirements — anything concrete/examples you can share will help speed procurement.

Appreciate it,
Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Product Risk, BrightBank

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@brightbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 13:48:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on default log retention (prompts vs outputs, caches, forensics)

Hi Oliver —

Thanks for the clear list — below are concise defaults for our hosted environment (EU region) and how they map to your SOW needs. I’ll include follow-ups for Dedicated/Private below as those differ.

1) What we store by default
- Prompts (user-submitted inputs): retained by default as request records. These are treated as customer "inputs" and are stored for 45 days (default) in hosted.
- Model completions (full finalized outputs): retained as artifacts, also 45 days by default.
- Streaming fragments / partial tokens: treated as transient buffers. We do not persist streaming fragments as finalized records by default; they are kept in an in-memory buffer and flushed only when finalized. For hosted, transient fragments are retained for up to 24 hours for debugging and then flushed. They are not indexed as separate artifacts.

2) KV cache and session state
- KV caches used to accelerate low-latency sessions are retained in a short-lived store. Default retention for those intermediate caches is 7 days in hosted (this is intended for session reconnection and short-term troubleshooting). They are not considered permanent artifacts and do not appear in customer-facing exports unless flagged during an incident.

3) Account-wide purge & deletion evidence
- Timeline: For hosted customers in EU, once we receive an authenticated purge request (via the Console + signed ticket) and complete our verification, Redwood completes object-level deletions within 72 hours. We then run a verification job and provide deletion evidence within the following 24 hours (signed summary + object manifest).
- Evidence we provide: a signed deletion summary (PDF) from our ops team, S3 delete markers / retention log entries (where applicable), and a manifest of object IDs/hashes that were removed. For Dedicated customers with an enterprise contract (SLA), we can commit to a 48-hour deletion window and provide an auditable report. For Private deployments (VPC / on-prem) retention and deletion are controlled by the customer; Redwood supports the runbook to perform deletions but cannot execute it unless explicitly contracted/authorized.

4) Opt-out controls
- Per-request: we support the header X-Redwood-Do-Not-Store: true which prevents persistent storage of prompts and outputs for that request in hosted API calls (note: some transient runtime state may remain briefly for request completion but is not written to persistent logs).
- Workspace flag: customers can enable a workspace-level "no-persist" mode for evaluation projects. If enabled, the default retention for that workspace is 0 days (no persistent artifacts), subject to audit/logging caveats for platform health.

Extras & examples:
- Embeddings: by default embeddings are stored if the customer calls the embeddings create API; retention follows workspace defaults (45 days hosted) unless the Do-Not-Store header is used.
- Forensics: our ops run a cryptographic manifest for every major purge that includes SHA256 hashes of object IDs with timestamps.

Attachments: I’ve attached our latest SOC 2 summary and a draft DPA (DocuSign link) for BrightBank procurement.

If you’d like, we can produce a short appendix with concrete JSON examples of the headers and a sample signed deletion summary to include in your SOW.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Security & Privacy PM, Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.ai

Thanks Hannah — that helps a lot. Two quick follow-ups from procurement/security: 

A) For Dedicated: can you confirm the 48-hour deletion SLA is available as an add-on in the standard enterprise contract, or does that require a bespoke clause?
B) For the Do-Not-Store header: will it also prevent storage of embeddings when present in the same request (we may batch evaluations that produce embeddings + text)?

We may need the sample deletion PDF and the header sample to circulate internally — can you drop those into a short example we can attach to our SOW?

Oliver

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@brightbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on default log retention (prompts vs outputs, caches, forensics)

Oliver —

A) Dedicated SLA: confirmed — 48-hour deletion and signed deletion report can be included in our standard enterprise addendum (no bespoke legal drafting required for most customers). We surface it as an optional SLA tier during procurement; procurement/finance usually selects it when the customer needs a tighter erasure commitment. I’ve looped Karthik (sales) and Kimberly (legal) to ensure procurement sees the standard clause language.

B) Do-Not-Store header behavior: the X-Redwood-Do-Not-Store: true header suppresses persistent storage for all artifacts created by that request, including generated text and embeddings. Two caveats: 1) if you have workspace-level analytics enabled we may retain aggregated metrics (non-reversible, aggregated counts) unless you opt out; 2) for streaming sessions some minimal transient state is used to complete the request but is not persisted.

Attachments included for procurement: a sample deletion summary in PDF format and a short API snippet you can paste into the SOW (see related links). If you want, we can run a 30-minute call with our infra folks to walk procurement/legal through the signed deletion example.

Next steps: if BrightBank confirms they want the 48-hour SLA, we’ll populate the addendum and provide the sample signed deletion PDF and header snippet within 24 hours.

—
